claims.statement: For every nonidentity P in G1 and every z in GT, the scheduled Pollard walk in proof.md recovers Q in G2 with e(P,Q)=z. Charging every Granger-Scott square, every dense Fp12 multiply, the shared squaring-backbone jump table, pairing setup, distinguished-point probes, verification and output, the walk uses at most 2^127.720581 target-group-operation equivalents. Under the random-image heuristic stated in proof.md the success probability on that step bound is at least 0.39 over uniform challenges and fresh algorithm coins. Peak memory is at most 2^121.917792 bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^21.000389 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in the total. Nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. No quantum step and no uncharged advice are used.

experiments.purpose: On a prime-order toy group, check that every collision of the windowed squaring-backbone schedule recovers the discrete log or is singular, and report the fraction of walks that collide within ceil(28/25 * sqrt(pi*order/2)) steps. A wrong logarithm aborts the run. This does not establish production field costs or the BLS12-381 heuristic extrapolation.
